headline: Sensex jumps over 500 points, Nifty nears 25,300 supported by FII buying and FMCG stocks

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign fund inflows and FII buying provided strong support to the domestic equity rally.
Strong performance in FMCG stocks helped drive the benchmark indices higher.
Early trade gains were led by key heavyweights including ITC, Airtel, and Asian Paints.
Morgan Stanley raised global equities to 'maximum overweight' citing earnings strength and cheap valuations.
whatHappening: Sensex surged over 500 points while Nifty 50 closed near 25,291.
RBI filed a review petition in the Supreme Court regarding YES Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT-1 bond case.
PNB featured among stocks hitting 52-week highs after rallying up to 24% in a month.
Sebi established an expert panel to review norms governing IPOs, FPOs, and capital-raising.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices closed sharply higher on November 16, with the Sensex advancing over 500 points to push Nifty near 25,300.
The gains were predominantly driven by foreign institutional inflows and strong buying interest in FMCG stocks.
Notable stock-specific actions included PNB touching a 52-week high, Max Healthcare emerging as a top gainer, and YES Bank facing regulatory news regarding its AT-1 bond case.
